rationale: First review of the accepted direct check fe65e174b269433b9d18622001fec470 (version 1) for obligation c-client-request-completes-on-inactive-raft. It supplies the required checker_correspondence item together with the applicability item, and resolves the two open input issues on this artifact's lineage (aa5f0ccb4bf14c69994ca8160b854bea on the claim and 0a5eff50ba8047dda64cef2f3a02bb7d on the fixed plan), each with a retained condition disposition. The reviewed execution is check fbb6404d8a05409a945aee193402861f: exit 0, completed, prerequisites matched, and the retained stdout shows 256 client calls to two shut-down nodes with 128 completed by ErrRaftShutdown and 128 returned futures that never completed (64 VerifyLeader, 64 batched Apply), while the unbuffered Barrier control completed 8 of 8.

review_items.rationale: The obligation under review says a client request against an inactive Raft node must complete - with ErrRaftShutdown or a real result - and must not leave the caller's future permanently unresolved; in particular, after Shutdown has returned, VerifyLeader and a batched Apply must not return a future whose Error() waits forever. The fixed check encodes exactly that. Its inputs are the package's own NewRaft over the in-memory store and transport, shut down through the public Shutdown(); because Shutdown().Error() calls waitShutdown, which waits for the goroutine group containing run, runFSM and runSnapshots (s-state-wait-shutdown, s-future-shutdown-future, s-raft-run-shutdown), the return of that call is the witness that no writer remains for the request channels, and the only producer of responses for verifyCh and applyCh is the main loop's verify and apply cases (s-raft-verify-mainloop). The check then exercises the default-configuration instance through VerifyLeader, whose channel is created with 64 slots (s-api-verify-leader, s-api-verify-ch-buffer), and the documented-option instance through Apply with BatchApplyCh, which buffers applyCh (s-api-apply-select, s-api-apply-buffer). Its oracle is a direct count: the harness reports raw per-path and total counts, and calls that returned ErrRaftShutdown are counted as completed (s-api-err-shutdown), so asserting unresolved_total equals zero is the requirement's own completion demand rather than a proxy, and the harness prints no verdict. The retained observation is nodes_inactive with all three nodes in state Shutdown followed by inactive_requests_observed with calls_total 256, completed_shutdown_total 128, completed_other_total 0, unresolved_verify 64, unresolved_apply 64, unresolved_total 128, and the control barrier at 8 of 8 completed; the test exited 0, so the violation is in the measured counts. The prerequisite nodes_inactive matched once in the single runner stream with the same setup and op identity and the admission has a later complete result, so the comparison is complete rather than a holds-only observation. The binding bind-raft-verify-leader locates the representative select structure at api.go VerifyLeader, and the second entry point and the control are cited by source ranges rather than by a second binding. Legality and observations were reviewed together: the harness reads each returned future's own completion channel non-blockingly and never calls Error(), which is sound only because the shutdown join has removed every writer, and the 250 ms wait is only corroboration - permanence is argued from the join, as the plan states. Counterevidence considered: with the default configuration Apply and Barrier are unbuffered, so they complete every time while the send case can never be ready, which is exactly what the control node measures (8 of 8 completed, 0 unresolved) and what separates the buffering of the channel from the API and the shutdown state; the select between an already-closed shutdown channel and a buffered send is a schedule choice, so the per-path counts vary between runs (64/64 here against 64/59 and 57/54 in construction runs) and a schedule in which every call took the shutdown branch would report holds, which the fixed prefix does not exclude; the in-repo TODO already records the same gap; and the reading that a caller racing shutdown carries the risk itself is kept as an alternative rather than as a refutation. What the check does not establish is listed in limitations.
limitations: Permanence rests on the shutdown join rather than on the measured wait: the 250 ms window only shows that the returned futures had not completed, and the argument that they never can is the waitShutdown ordering that the plan states as legality.

The select is a schedule choice, so the unresolved counts vary between runs and the prefix does not exclude a schedule in which every call takes the shutdown branch; only that schedule's vanishing probability separates the observed violation from a holds result.

The batched instance depends on the documented BatchApplyCh option; with the default unbuffered applyCh the same select can never take the send case, which is why the control is included and why the batched failure is not evidence about Apply under the default configuration.

Only the VerifyLeader and ApplyLog entry points are exercised; the snapshot, bootstrap, configuration-change and restore channels are unbuffered in the captured source, and a request enqueued before shutdown rather than issued after it is outside the prefix.

The harness observes live futures through their own channels and deliberately does not call Error(), so it measures non-completion at one point after the shutdown join plus the bounded wait rather than consuming any late response.
review_items.report_title: 停机后的客户端请求可永久不完成
review_items.report_answer: 对两个已 Shutdown 完成的节点发起 256 次公开客户端调用后，128 次立即返回 ErrRaftShutdown，另 128 次返回的 future 始终没有完成（VerifyLeader 64 次、BatchApplyCh 下的 Apply 64 次），而使用默认无缓冲通道的 Barrier 对照 8/8 全部完成。测试以退出码 0 结束，因此违规体现在被测量的未完成计数上，而非退出码；永久性由 Shutdown().Error() 已等待 goroutine 组退出这一事实支撑。

review_items.rationale: The library owes this completion duty in the selected scope for four sourced reasons. First, ErrRaftShutdown is documented as the result of operations requested against an inactive Raft (s-api-err-shutdown) and the in-repo after-shutdown test states that everything should fail now (s-test-after-shutdown). Second, the library owns both writers and the shutdown ordering: responses for these requests come only from the main loop's verify and apply cases (s-raft-verify-mainloop), while Shutdown closes the shutdown channel and shutdownFuture.Error joins the goroutine group (s-state-wait-shutdown, s-future-shutdown-future). Third, the library chooses the buffering that makes the failure reachable: verifyCh is created with 64 slots in NewRaft (s-api-verify-ch-buffer) and applyCh is buffered whenever the documented BatchApplyCh option is set (s-api-apply-buffer), so with the shutdown channel already closed both select cases can be ready and the request is enqueued rather than rejected (s-api-verify-leader, s-api-apply-select). Fourth, the returned future has no alternate escape, because deferError consults only errCh and ShutdownCh and neither logFuture nor verifyFuture sets ShutdownCh (s-future-defer-error). The retained condition points out that the same in-repo test whose assertion covers Apply and the configuration APIs also carries a TODO recording that Barrier, VerifyLeader and GetConfiguration can get stuck instead. That is a known-gap acknowledgment inside the same source, not counterevidence against the duty: it confirms that the intended outcome is failure rather than an unresolved future, and it leaves only the repair location open, so it is retained as an independent scope boundary. The same reading applies to the stricter form of the condition recorded on the fixed plan, which adds the buffering evidence; neither form changes what the library owes, because in both the test's assertion and the TODO describe the same intended completion behavior and the observed behavior violates it.
limitations: The repair location is undecided and retained as an independent boundary: draining the buffered channels during shutdown, setting deferError.ShutdownCh for these futures, and stopping the send case once shutdown is signalled are all consistent with the duty.

The documented sentence about operations against an inactive Raft does not settle whether a caller that races Shutdown rather than calling after it is covered; this review treats the after-shutdown case as in scope and keeps the racing case as an open boundary.
The duty is established for the two buffered request channels exercised here; the unbuffered request channels of the captured source are not claimed to share it.
review_items.report_title: 停机完成后的请求完成义务成立
review_items.report_answer: ErrRaftShutdown 的文档语义、仓库内停机测试的意图、库自身对缓冲通道与停机顺序的控制，以及 future 只有 errCh 一条完成路径，共同确立了该义务适用于本范围；同一测试中的 TODO 只是承认当前实现会卡住，并未否定请求应当完成，也不改变修复位置之外的责任。

resolutions.rationale: The condition records that the in-repo after-shutdown test asserts everything should fail while its TODO says Barrier, VerifyLeader and GetConfiguration can get stuck. The applicability answer separates intent from implementation: the assertion states the duty that operations against an inactive Raft complete with ErrRaftShutdown (s-api-err-shutdown), the TODO records that the current implementation does not always achieve it, and the library controls everything that decides which happens - the buffered channels it creates (s-api-verify-ch-buffer, s-api-apply-buffer), the select that can choose the send after shutdown (s-api-verify-leader, s-api-apply-select, s-api-barrier-select), the goroutine join that follows (s-state-wait-shutdown, s-future-shutdown-future) and the futures' single completion channel (s-future-defer-error). The check then observed the failure under the documented contract: 256 calls against nodes whose Shutdown completed returned 128 ErrRaftShutdown results and 128 futures that never completed, with the unbuffered barrier control completing 8 of 8 (check fbb6404d8a05409a945aee193402861f of artifact fe65e174b269433b9d18622001fec470). The acknowledgment is therefore retained as an independent boundary - it identifies that the repair is outstanding and where it might go - rather than being treated as a discharge of the obligation.
scope_limitations: The repair location stays open: draining buffered channels on shutdown, giving these futures a shutdown escape, or never offering the send case once shutdown is signalled are all consistent with the duty.
The control and the cited sources cover the two buffered request channels exercised here; unbuffered request channels are not claimed to share the failure.

condition_dispositions.rationale: This condition records an in-repo acknowledgment of the same gap the obligation names. It does not remove the duty: the assertion states the intended completion behavior, the TODO states that the implementation violates it, and the library owns the channel buffering, the shutdown join and the futures' completion path. It is retained as an independent boundary describing where the repair remains outstanding.

resolutions.rationale: The plan-level condition is the same acknowledgment read against the fixed check's legality: the fixed inputs, not the assertion, are what the TODO qualifies. The plan therefore retains the acknowledgment in its legality conflicts and states that the observed behavior violates the intended contract rather than that the contract is absent, and the check demonstrates the reachable instance on the fixed inputs - verifyCh built with 64 slots (s-api-verify-ch-buffer), applyCh buffered by the documented option (s-api-apply-buffer), a shutdown join that leaves no responder (s-state-wait-shutdown, s-future-shutdown-future, s-raft-run-shutdown), the main loop as the only responder (s-raft-verify-mainloop) and futures without a shutdown escape (s-future-defer-error). The retained execution shows 128 of 256 calls never completing while the unbuffered control completes every call, so the condition does not invalidate the fixed inputs and remains an open boundary about the repair. Resolving it here keeps the acknowledgment attached to the answering version of the plan rather than silently dropping it.
scope_limitations: The condition is answered as an outstanding-repair boundary on the fixed inputs; the plan's own recorded limits (schedule choice, BatchApplyCh dependence, prefix boundaries) remain independently visible.
No claim is made that the fixed plan covers unbuffered request channels or requests enqueued before shutdown.

condition_dispositions.rationale: This condition qualifies the fixed check by recording that the in-repo test's TODO already knows the completion gap. The fixed inputs still exercise the requirement's premise - buffered request channels and a completed shutdown join - and the observation is a violation of the intended completion behavior, so the acknowledgment is retained as an independent boundary about the outstanding repair rather than as a reason to reject the inputs.
